title: When the Group Chat Breaks
premise: Ines Ashgrove has spent fifteen years being the careful one — the baker's kid who kneads grief into sourdough and never says what they mean. When their best friend Marisol vanishes, leaving only a ring of keys and a half-deleted group chat, Ines discovers the keys open doors all over town: a shuttered courthouse annex, a records office, a room where someone has been documenting every injustice the town's powerful families buried. As Ines and three other chat members follow the trail, they realize Marisol wasn't taken — she was running an underground archive of the town's crimes, and now the people she exposed are hunting her. Ines must choose between turning over the evidence to save Marisol legally (and letting the guilty walk) or releasing it themselves and becoming outlaws. In the end, Ines publishes everything at dawn, finds Marisol hiding in plain sight, and finally bakes bread that tastes like who they actually are.
about_author: Kestrel Coldharbour grew up above a bakery in a small river town and still believes secrets rise better in warm dough. They write young adult novels about kids who fix what adults broke, usually before breakfast.

chapters.title: The Last Read Receipt
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A normal Friday: closing the bakery, group chat banter, Marisol promising to bring 'the thing' tomorrow. Then Marisol stops replying mid-sentence. Ines rereads the messages until 3 a.m., telling themself it's nothing. Emotional beat: dread disguised as denial; the reader feels the silence arrive before Ines admits it.

chapters.title: A Ring of Keys on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. On the bakery step at dawn: Marisol's keyring, seven unfamiliar keys, no note. Ines calls the police, who file it as a runaway case because Marisol is seventeen. Ines posts in the group chat; only Theo answers. Beat: the first crack between official justice and real justice.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Silence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The chat members meet in person for the first time: Ines, anxious archivist Theo, sharp-tongued Priya, and quiet Jonah, who knew Marisol longest and says least. They inventory the keys. One fits the old courthouse annex door. Beat: reluctant alliance forming around shared worry.

chapters.title: What the Annex Kept
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Inside the annex: dust, folding chairs, and a wall of pinned documents — decades of covered-up wrongs by the Halloway family, who own half the town. The newest page is dated last week, in Marisol's handwriting. Beat: awe curdling into fear; Marisol wasn't lost, she was working.

chapters.title: Bread for People Who Won't Eat
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines can't sleep, so they bake — cinnamon loaves shaped like apology — and delivers them to each friend. Priya reveals Marisol asked her about public records laws two months ago. Beat: tenderness as coping mechanism; Ines's baking shown as their true language.

chapters.title: The Halloway Smile
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Councilman Aldous Halloway visits the bakery, buys nothing, and mentions he hears Ines has been 'poking around municipal property.' He leaves a business card and a threat dressed as courtesy. Beat: the antagonist enters gently, which makes him worse.

chapters.title: Key Number Four
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Key four opens a storage unit: Marisol's go-bag, cash, a burner phone, and a printed itinerary ending the night she vanished. She planned to leave — but something made her stay or get stopped. Beat: hope and betrayal tangled; did Marisol abandon them or protect them?

chapters.title: The Group Chat Breaks
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Someone screenshots the chat and sends it to all four parents. Priya's mother forbids her involvement; Jonah goes silent; Theo's parents threaten to report the annex break-in themselves. Beat: the found family fractures under adult pressure — duty versus loyalty.

chapters.title: Ines, Uncareful
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Cornered by their father, who begs them to let the police handle it, Ines finally shouts the truth they've swallowed for fifteen years: careful never saved anyone. They walk out mid-shift, apron still on. Beat: the protagonist's defining rupture with obedience.

chapters.title: Records Room Ghosts
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Using her research skills, Priya traces the annex documents to a 1998 fire officially ruled accidental — the same week a Halloway warehouse burned with a worker inside. Marisol had found the witness statement everyone thought was destroyed. Beat: the past becomes a weapon and a warning.

chapters.title: Jonah Knew
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah confesses: Marisol told him everything weeks ago and swore him to secrecy because his father works for Halloway. His silence was protection, he says. Ines doesn't forgive him yet. Beat: betrayal reframed as love against duty — and still a wound.

chapters.title: The Burner Rings
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The burner phone from the storage unit rings. A stranger's voice: 'You have her keys. She wants you to stop looking.' But background sound — flour sifters, oven timers — places the caller near the old mill district. Beat: terror sharpened into a lead.

chapters.title: Mill District, After Curfew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The remaining three (Priya defies her mother) search the mill ruins and find signs someone lived there recently: blankets, canned food, chalk arrows matching Marisol's handwriting style. She was hiding, not held. Beat: relief and new fear — if she's hiding, who is she hiding from?

chapters.title: Halloway Makes It Legal
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Halloway obtains a court order declaring the teens trespassers and the annex evidence 'stolen property,' scheduled for destruction Friday. The law itself is now the threat. Beat: the theme crystallizes — justice outside the law because the law has been bought.

chapters.title: What Ines Bakes for Traitors
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah offers to use his father's access to copy Halloway's private files. Ines, still angry, tests him with a task that could expose them both. He passes. Beat: forgiveness begins as action, not words; trust rebuilt in the dark.

chapters.title: The Father's Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Jonah's copied files include payments to the fire investigator of 1998 and, worse, a recent invoice: 'asset retrieval, one subject.' Marisol didn't run — she was caught and got away. Beat: stakes become physical; the clock starts ticking loudly.

chapters.title: Where You Hide a Girl Who Reads Everything
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines realizes Marisol's chalk arrows match the numbering system of the town library's closed stacks — where the two of them hid as children during fire drills. They go alone, not trusting anyone else with the location. Beat: intimacy of shared history; love as navigation.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV (first time). Found thin and fierce in the stacks, she explains: she stayed to finish copying the archive before fleeing, but Halloway's man cornered her; she escaped through the book drop and has been moving nightly since. She's terrified — and refuses to hand the archive to police. Beat: reunion undercut by conflict; the friends' goals split.

chapters.title: Two Doors Out
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group argues: give the archive to a journalist Marisol distrusts, or publish it themselves tonight before Friday's destruction order. Halloway's man is spotted circling the block. Marisol votes publish; Ines hesitates — until realizing waiting means losing everything twice. Beat: the decision point; duty and love pull opposite directions and love wins.

chapters.title: Publish at Dawn
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. From the bakery's ancient computer, they upload the entire archive to a hundred mirrors, email every regional newsroom, and print copies for the courthouse steps. Halloway's man pounds on the bakery door as the progress bar fills. Beat: climax — the most careful person in town chooses, irrevocably, to be brave.

chapters.title: The Town That Read Everything
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. By noon the story is everywhere; state investigators arrive; Halloway resigns behind a wall of cameras. There are costs: Theo's parents are furious, Priya's mother is quietly proud, Jonah's father loses his job. Marisol comes down the hill with her hands visible. Beat: aftermath without neatness — justice arrived, imperfectly, outside the law.

chapters.title: Bread That Tastes Like Me
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Weeks later: the five friends reopen the annex as a community archive. Ines bakes a loaf with no recipe, no care for how it looks, and gives the first slice to Marisol. It tastes, they decide, like belonging. Final beat: the labels come off, and what's underneath was worth the wait.
